title: Consistent symmetry breaking and topological phases
abstract: Operators invariant under a symmetry group are also invariant under any finite-index subgroup. The equivariant indices of such operators must be consistent under symmetry breaking. We use this principle to establish a canonical weak/strong dichotomy for equivariant indices, building on an idea originating in the theory of topological insulators in solid-state physics. We also study the relationship to coarse-geometric, or macroscopic, indices.
summary: This work develops a rigorous mathematical theory to classify topological phases by analyzing how symmetry breaking affects the index of Dirac-type operators. It introduces a weak/strong dichotomy for these indices, generalizing concepts from solid-state physics into abstract settings involving group $C^*$-algebras and coarse geometry.
main_problem: The paper establishes a general mathematical framework for defining topological invariants (indices) that remain consistent under symmetry breaking, particularly in settings involving proper metric spaces and discrete group actions.
main_result: It develops a canonical weak/strong dichotomy for equivariant indices and relates these abstract algebraic structures to macroscopic or coarse-geometric indices derived from the system's underlying geometry.
method: The methodology combines advanced concepts from K-theory, index theory (specifically involving Dirac-type operators), and coarse geometry applied to $C^*$-algebras associated with group actions.
model_or_system: The theoretical framework is motivated by solid-state physics models like topological insulators, where Hamiltonians are $\Gamma$-invariant Schrödinger or Dirac operators on a space $X$ acted upon by a discrete group $\Gamma$.
key_observables: Equivariant indices ($	ext{ind}_\Gamma(/D)$) and the resulting weak/strong K-theory classes that characterize topological phases.
important_parameters: The structure of the symmetry group $\Gamma$ (e.g., abelian lattices $\mathbb{Z}^d$) and the nature of the space $X$.
main_assumptions: Requires $X$ to be a proper metric space with a proper, cocompact action of $\Gamma$, and relies on constructing specific Roe algebras associated with this geometry.
figures_summary: Figure 1.1 illustrates 'coarse-graining' by showing how an orbit under $\mathbb{Z}_2$ is lumped together in a coarse-grained fundamental domain when symmetry is broken to $2\mathbb{Z}_2$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the index for operators invariant under symmetries, formalizing symmetry breaking via finite-index subgroups and associated colimits, establishing the weak/strong dichotomy, and relating this structure to coarse-geometric indices.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the connection between topological invariants derived from spectral theory (like those in condensed matter) and deep algebraic structures like K-theory and group $C^*$-algebras provides powerful mathematical tools for classifying quantum phases of matter.

figures.caption: Figure 1.1. In the left diagram, the large black circles indicate an orbit for the standard Z2-action on R2, while the shaded 1 × 1 square indicates a fundamental domain. Symmetry breaking to 2Z2 is depicted by the top diagram — the shaded 2 × 2 square in- dicates a “coarse-grained” fundamental domain containing a single point of the 2Z2-orbit (large black circle). Points of the Z2-orbit (small black circles) are no longer individually distinguished, but are lumped together in fours. We may also break Z2 to 2Z × 3Z (bottom) or 6Z2 (right); the latter breaking can be done in two stages in several different ways (upper arrows or lower arrows).
